title: Introduce ephemeral controlplane nexthop orchestrator and Route53 DNS safelist
author: Alexandra Chen
description:
Context: customers running Redwood Private in complex VPC topologies have asked for a way to route control-plane egress through short-lived, auditable nexthops (ENIs/ephemeral NAT targets) to reduce blast radius during upgrades and to provide deterministic routing for IAM/Route53 forwarding. This PR introduces an ephemeral nexthop orchestrator in the installer and a companion Route53 "DNS safelist" mechanism that stages DNS outbound endpoints and limits TTL exposure during controlled switchover.
Motivation: (1) enable safe, staged control plane egress migration across AZs/accounts, (2) provide a fast rollback path that avoids long DNS TTL propagation, (3) improve security by narrowing SG scopes to ephemeral nexthops and recording ephemeral credentials in audit logs.
Summary of changes:
- Terraform: new module network/ephemeral-nexthop that provisions an ENI-backed nexthop, EIP attachment, IAM role for the installer agent, and tags used for lifecycle reconciliation.
- Installer operator (Go): added a reconciler that creates nexthop resources, assigns SGs based on policy templates, and emits provenance events to the control-plane audit sink. The reconciler supports a "staged" lifecycle (provision -> drain -> swap -> cleanup).
- Helm charts: added values.controlplane.nexthop and an optional preflight job chart to validate egress path and DNS behavior.
- Route53 tooling: implement a DNS safelist controller that creates temporary outbound endpoints and manages a small Route53 record-set swap (low TTL priming, atomic CNAME flip).
- Tests & CI: integration tests in perf-canary that simulate switchover, unit tests for the reconciler, and a Terraform plan check in CI.
Checklist:
- [x] Add Terraform module and docs
- [x] Implement reconciler + helm values
- [x] Add unit and integration tests
- [x] Manual QA in staging (AZ failover + peering teardown scenario)
- [x] Security review for IAM/SG changes
Rollout plan:
1) Deploy module with Helm values disabled (no-op) to ensure no drift.
2) Enable module in a single staging region and run the preflight job.
3) Execute staged switchover with traffic mirroring and monitor console metrics/traces.
4) If safe, enable in production with canary subset of control-plane nodes.
Rollback notes: reconcilers keep ownership tags and will revert to previous nexthop if swap fails; DNS safelist controller reverts CNAMEs and shortens TTL to accelerate rollback. See notes_on_rollback below for details.
CI: initial run failed on plan due to missing IAM trust for the installer agent; fixed by adding a narrowly scoped assume-role policy and re-ran CI.
Merge outcome: squash merge after security and infra approvals.
Related Linear items: ENG-3187 (nexthop orchestration), ENG-3219 (DNS safelist), ENG-3223 (release rollouts).
commits: 5 commits: add terraform module scaffold; implement reconciler core loop; add helm values + preflight job; route53 safelist controller; tests and docs
review_comments: Ravi Patel: Please narrow the installer-agent assume-role policy to only List/Attach/Describe for the ENI resources. Also add a unit test for tag collision handling.
Author (Alexandra Chen): Addressed — policy trimmed, added TestTagCollision to reconciler_test.go and documented the expected ownership tag format.
Maria Gomez: The DNS safelist controller should default to TTL=30s for priming records to reduce propagation risk. Can we make TTL configurable?
Author (Alexandra Chen): TTL is now configurable via values.controlplane.nexthop.dnsPrimeTTLSeconds with default 30. Updated docs and Helm values.
Jordan Kim: Can we add a metric for the number of active ephemeral nexthops and expose it in the console?
Author (Alexandra Chen): Added prometheus gauge installer_nexthop_active_count and wired chart to expose metric in Redwood Console.
release_notes: Added an optional ephemeral nexthop orchestrator and a Route53 DNS safelist primitive for safe control-plane egress migration. Operators can stage switchover with low TTL priming and fast rollback. Requires opt-in via helm values.
notes_on_rollback: Reconciler retains the previous nexthop resource for 10 minutes after attempted swap. DNS safelist controller keeps a record of old CNAME targets and will revert atomically; short TTLs accelerate propagation. To force rollback: trigger the installer reconciler with annotation installer.redwood.ai/rollback=true and the controller will reattach the previous EIP and flip DNS back.
testing_summary: Unit tests cover tag reconciliation and lifecycle transitions. Integration test in perf-canary deploys two nexthops, simulates peering teardown, validates path, and verifies Route53 swap behavior. Manual verification performed in staging (us-west-2) with canary control-plane nodes. Observability: traces added to the reconciler span out to the control-plane console and Prometheus metrics were validated.
